extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of 37,200 English multiple-choice math word problems densely annotated with formal operation programs.
extraction.creator: Aida Amini (University of Washington); Saadia Gabriel (University of Washington); Shanchuan Lin (University of Washington); Rik Koncel-Kedziorski (University of Washington); Yejin Choi (University of Washington; Allen Institute for AI); Hannaneh Hajishirzi (University of Washington; Allen Institute for AI)
extraction.citeAs: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, and Hannaneh Hajishirzi. MathQA: Towards Interpretable Math Word Problem Solving with Operation-Based Formalisms. arXiv:1905.13319v1, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by selecting math word problems from the existing AQuA dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The source AQuA dataset contained noise, including problems with incorrect solutions, unsolvable problems, and rationales that contained few or none of the steps required to solve the corresponding problem.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The AQuA (AQUA-RAT) dataset, which provides over 100K GRE- and GMAT-level multiple-choice math word problems.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers were provided with a problem description, a list of operations related to the problem category, and a list of valid arguments, and iteratively selected operations and arguments until the problem was solved. Annotators were evaluated through test questions and had to maintain an accuracy threshold.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A validation strategy was used to check whether the problems and annotated programs were aligned, requiring at least 2 out of 3 validators to rank the operation program as valid for it to be selected.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The representation language lacks certain operations like factorization; the categorization strategy is slightly noisy; some problems lack sufficient textual context or contain erroneous text; excludes non-narrative problems and those requiring brute-force rather than logical reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating deep neural models for math word problem solving and logical reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We find closely similar problems, replace numeric values with generic numbers, and expand annotations to cover more problems from the AQuA dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problems that can only be solved by brute-force instead of logical reasoning and non-narrative problems that do not fit the definition of a math word problem (in Table 2 these appear as “no word”) are removed from consideration.
